evidence:
At b = nu the single-neuron budget is known.

(1) Morwani et al., ICLR 2024 (arXiv 2311.07568). PDF read in full; the cyclic proof of Thm 7 is in the appendix, eqs. (6)-(9).
- For the quadratic neuron, the expected class-weighted margin is 2/((p-1)p^2) sum_{j!=0} u^(j)v^(j)w^(-j).
- Plancherel gives "||u^||^2+||v^||^2+||w^||^2 <= p".
- "By the inequality of quadratic and geometric means" (eq. 9): |u^||v^||w^| <= (z(j)/3)^{3/2}.
- Cauchy-Schwarz with ||z||_2 <= ||z||_1 then gives sqrt(2/27)/(p^{1/2}(p-1)).
- Equality holds only for balanced single-frequency cosines.
- Lemma 18 is the group analogue: AM-GM on Frobenius norms.
This is our AM-GM / superadditivity / Parseval argument at n=2, b=nu=3.

(2) Li, Liang, Shi, Song, Zhou, AISTATS 2025, PMLR 258:523-531 (arXiv 2402.09469). PDF read in full.
- Lemma D.7: the power neuron (sum u_i)^k w reduces to k!/((p-1)p^k) sum_j w^(-j) prod u^_i(j). This is exactly our "only the multilinear monomial survives, with coefficient n!".
- Lemma D.8 (formal Lemma 4.2): QM-GM, then max_{||z||_1<=p/2} sum z^{(k+1)/2} <= (p/2)^{(k+1)/2}. The value is 2(k!)/((2k+2)^{(k+1)/2}(p-1)p^{(k-1)/2}) = n! B_p * p/(p-1), attained by balanced single-frequency cosines.

New in our result:
- The b < nu generalisation: exponent b/nu, with the value B_p independent of b. It uses the same three steps with t^{b/2} superadditive, so it is a routine extension.
- The observation that a neuron can carry many frequencies at no extra cost when b = 2.
- The ReLU bound C_2 <= p^{-n}/2 (Lipschitz-variance argument). No precedent found; Morwani and Li treat ReLU only empirically.

Side findings:
- li2025nsum is in refs.bib but is cited nowhere in the sections. Its only mention is a TODO at intro.tex:22.
- The power-neuron "<= n! B_p" appears attainable as an equality at every b by the same cosine witness. Li D.8 confirms this at b = nu for all k.

recommended_citations.why: Supports approach.tex l.54 ('as in Morwani, a single-neuron optimization'). Their appendix eqs. (6)-(9) prove the n=2, b=nu=3 case of C_b by QM-GM + Plancherel + ||z||_2<=||z||_1, with the same equality case: a balanced single-frequency cosine.

Lemma D.7 is our power-neuron 'only the multilinear term, with coefficient n!' step. Lemma D.8 is the b=nu budget for general k: QM-GM plus sum z^{(k+1)/2} <= (p/2)^{(k+1)/2}, with maximum 2(k!)/((2k+2)^{(k+1)/2}(p-1)p^{(k-1)/2}) = n! B_p Gamma_1(p). Cite it in app:models, power-neuron paragraph. It is currently in refs.bib but cited nowhere.
